explanation: The trachea divides into two primary bronchi, which enter the right and left lungs. Inside the lungs, the bronchi branch repeatedly into smaller tubes called bronchioles. Each bronchiole terminates in an elongated air space enclosed by clusters of microscopic, thin-walled air sacs called alveoli. Gas exchange occurs by diffusion across the thin walls of the alveoli and the surrounding network of pulmonary capillaries.

questions.q: Into what two tubes does the trachea divide at its base?
questions.exp: The trachea divides to form two primary bronchi, which enter the left and right lungs.

questions.q: Where does gas exchange take place in human lungs?
opts: Across the walls of the alveoli and adjacent capillaries
questions.exp: Alveoli are the microscopic, thin-walled air sacs where oxygen diffuses into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out.
